story1_chart_a.notes: Notebook's printed monthly table (cell 5, `monthly.tail(8)`) only shows Jun 2017 - Jan 2018 verbatim -- it does not print the full Jan2017-Jan2018 series the brief asked for, only this 8-month tail. Used exactly what was printed rather than extending the range with unverified numbers or recomputing from the raw CSV. This 8-month window already shows the full pattern clearly: items/order flat ~3.0 through Sep 2017, then falls to exactly 1.0 by Nov 2017; order value flat ~$615-664, falls to $156 by Jan 2018. Vertical break marker placed at Nov 2017 per spec, even though the drop is visibly already underway in Oct 2017's partial figures (1.07 items/order, $511 order value).

story1_chart_b.notes: All 13 quarterly margin_pct values pulled verbatim from the notebook's printed quarterly summary table (cell 5). Margin = Order Profit Per Order / Order Item Total. No visible step change at the Nov 2017 (Q4 2017) boundary -- Q4 2017 (12.46%) and Q1 2018 (11.36%) both sit comfortably inside the pre-artifact 10.79%-12.73% band, confirming the notebook's own takeaway that margin is undistorted by the order-composition artifact.

story2_chart_a.notes: Placeholder ranks (9 and 26) matched exactly what the notebooks print. 0.4_prod_region_cross.ipynb originally found this using margin = profit/Sales (naive_mean 11.43%, weighted 10.35%, same 9->26 rank shift). 1_cardio_equipment_cost_driver.ipynb section 1 redid the comparison with the corrected denominator (profit/Order Item Total, the archive's standard) and confirmed the identical rank shift (naive 12.73%, weighted 11.51%, rank 9 -> 26 of 32 qualifying categories), so the corrected numbers are used here per the task instructions.

numbers.sku: Nike Men's Free 5.0+ Running Shoe (Cardio Equipment's dominant SKU, 97.4% of category order lines)

story2_chart_b.notes: IMPORTANT DEVIATION FROM SPEC: the notebook shows 5 markets (Africa, LATAM, Europe, Pacific Asia, USCA), not the 4 named in the brief -- Cardio Equipment sells in all 5 of the dataset's Market values, and LATAM is a real fifth data point sitting between Africa and the other three on both volume and margin. Used all 5 real markets rather than dropping LATAM to force-fit 4. Chart values are `margin_pct` (total profit / total revenue per market, the notebook's headline metric); the notebook's prose also mentions an alternate ~15.5% figure for Africa which is `avg_profit_ratio` (mean of the per-order-line ratio field, a slightly different aggregation) -- the 14.516% weighted margin_pct was used for consistency with the other 4 markets and with the archive's standard margin definition.

story3_chart_a.source_notebook: 2_fraud_late_delivery_exposure.ipynb (primary; Late delivery/Suspected fraud/Canceled/company average) + 1_cardio_equipment_cost_driver.ipynb cell 11 (Normal/on-time figure)
story3_chart_a.notes: 2_fraud_late_delivery_exposure.ipynb prints Late delivery risk=1 margin (11.74%), SUSPECTED_FRAUD margin (11.27%), CANCELED margin (12.61%), and company average (12.04%) directly (section 1). It does NOT isolate an on-time-only margin figure. The 'Normal (on-time)' bar (12.20%) is pulled from 1_cardio_equipment_cost_driver.ipynb cell 11, which prints company-wide margin by Late_delivery_risk (0 -> 12.20%, 1 -> 11.91%) on the same filtered/clean dataset and same margin definition, using a slightly different aggregation (mean of per-row ratios rather than sum-of-profit/sum-of-revenue) -- hence the small difference between its late-delivery figure (11.91%) and 2_fraud's (11.74%); the 2_fraud figure was used for the Late delivery bar since that notebook is the designated primary source. All four bars land within about 1 percentage point of the 12.04% company average, which is exactly the point of this chart.

story3_chart_b.notes: Two-panel layout used as suggested (fraud rate left, late-delivery rate right) since the two metrics have different scales. Reference lines (2.1% fraud, 54.6% late) are the notebook's own printed unweighted across-region average figures (used in its z-score calc and prose), not the order-weighted company-wide rates (2.25% fraud / 54.8% late) printed elsewhere in the same notebook -- used the region-average figures since those are what the z-scores in this chart are actually measured against. Canada appears in both panels (highest raw fraud rate but a less extreme z-score of 1.87, so colored as 'notably worse' on fraud; lowest late-delivery rate by far at z=-3.63, colored as the 'better than average' standout, gray).

story5_chart_a.notes: Both the mean lifetime spend by tier and the tier-to-tier step-up (added value) tables pulled verbatim from the notebook's printed output (cell 34). Step-up bounces $455-$865 with mean ~$570 and no trend, confirming additive (not accelerating) LTV growth -- matches the brief's ~$530-610 placeholder range closely, with tier 10 (open-ended 10+) showing more noise as expected from a smaller sample (n=258).

story5_chart_b.notes: Numbers pulled verbatim from the notebook's printed combo table (cell 26): baseline top-15% rate 15.1% (cell 22); the 4 conditions used in the chart are baseline, 'reorder without matching spend' (below-median 90-day spend + reordered = 9.9%, closely matching the brief's ~9.9% placeholder exactly), 'above-median spend alone' (no reorder = 15.5%), and the standout combined condition (above-median spend + early reorder = 25.7%, matching the brief's ~25.7% placeholder exactly). The notebook's 5th cell (below-median spend, no reorder = 8.7%) was omitted from the chart as the weakest/reference condition, matching the brief's 4-bar spec.

story6_chart.notes: Both curves pulled verbatim from the notebook's printed dicts (cell 20: `order_view['n_lines']` and `shuf_view`). The near-identical inverted-U shape between real and randomly-shuffled discount assignment is the notebook's core finding: the apparent 6-15%-discount 'sweet spot' is regression-to-the-mean on order-level average-of-random-draws, not a real behavioral threshold effect.
